newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends mixed on pre-weekend swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends mixed on pre-weekend swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly weaker on Wednesday due to swaps ahead of the forthcoming long weekend, but had regained some ground lost earlier on falling long bond yields, traders said.
"When dealers saw the U.S. long bond firm up, they sold some dollars they had bought recently," a trader said. "Some swapped to 48-hour contracts ahead of the weekend."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.9 and 0.6 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.9500/7.9520 and 7.9380/7.9420 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile up 15/32 to yield 6.95 percent.
Dealers said dealers tended to sell dollars in the same-day market to buy back at 48 hours using pesos that may be invested in the money market until settlement is due next Tuesday.
Mexican financial markets will be closed on Thursday, May 1, for Labor Day, and to commemorate the battle of Puebla on Monday, May 5.
Traders said demand for peso instruments had driven down overnight Cetes rates by 125 basis points to 17.50 percent.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 3.6 centavos firmer at 7.9280/7.9320 per dollar.
Dealers said trading on Friday would depend on the U.S. bond market's reaction to U.S. employment and unemployment data.
